metadata.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms (Schulman, Wolski, Dhariwal, Radford, Klimov, 2017)
metadata.venue: arXiv preprint (widely cited as OpenAI tech report)
metadata.framework: policy optimization via clipped surrogate objective as alternative to trust-region constraint
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1707.06347. No LaTeX source downloaded.

nodes.name: Policy gradient and REINFORCE estimator
nodes.statement: The policy gradient theorem gives $\hat{g} = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t \left[ \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t | s_t) \hat{A}_t \right]$ where $\hat{A}_t$ is an estimator of the advantage function at timestep $t$ and the expectation is over a finite batch of trajectories.

nodes.name: Probability ratio $r_t(\theta)$
nodes.statement: The probability ratio between the new and old policies: $r_t(\theta) = \frac{\pi_\theta(a_t | s_t)}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(a_t | s_t)}$. Note $r_t(\theta_{\text{old}}) = 1$. The surrogate objective from TRPO can be written as $L^{\mathrm{CPI}}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t \left[ r_t(\theta) \hat{A}_t \right]$.

nodes.name: Clipped surrogate objective $L^{\mathrm{CLIP}}$
nodes.statement: The clipped surrogate objective: $L^{\mathrm{CLIP}}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t \left[ \min\left( r_t(\theta) \hat{A}_t, \; \mathrm{clip}(r_t(\theta), 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon) \hat{A}_t \right) \right]$ where $\epsilon > 0$ (e.g., $\epsilon = 0.2$) is a hyperparameter. The clipping removes the incentive for moving $r_t$ outside $[1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon]$, providing a pessimistic (lower) bound on the unclipped objective.

nodes.name: Adaptive KL penalty coefficient (PPO-Penalty variant)
nodes.statement: An alternative to clipping: $L^{\mathrm{KLPEN}}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t \left[ r_t(\theta) \hat{A}_t - \beta \, D_{\mathrm{KL}}[\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(\cdot|s_t) \| \pi_\theta(\cdot|s_t)] \right]$ where $\beta$ is adapted: if $d = D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}, \pi_\theta) < d_{\mathrm{targ}} / 1.5$, halve $\beta$; if $d > d_{\mathrm{targ}} \times 1.5$, double $\beta$.

nodes.name: Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE)
nodes.statement: The advantage estimator used in PPO is GAE($\lambda$): $\hat{A}_t = \sum_{l=0}^{T-t} (\gamma \lambda)^l \delta_{t+l}$ where $\delta_t = r_t + \gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t)$ is the TD residual. This interpolates between TD(0) ($\lambda=0$) and Monte Carlo ($\lambda=1$).

nodes.name: Combined objective with value and entropy
nodes.statement: The full PPO objective maximized at each iteration: $L^{\mathrm{CLIP+VF+S}}_t(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t \left[ L^{\mathrm{CLIP}}_t(\theta) - c_1 L^{\mathrm{VF}}_t(\theta) + c_2 S[\pi_\theta](s_t) \right]$ where $L^{\mathrm{VF}}_t = (V_\theta(s_t) - V_t^{\mathrm{targ}})^2$ is the value-function loss, $S$ is the entropy bonus, and $c_1, c_2$ are coefficients.

nodes.name: PPO algorithm (minibatch SGD on clipped objective)
nodes.statement: The PPO algorithm: (1) Run $N$ parallel actors for $T$ timesteps collecting trajectories. (2) Compute advantages $\hat{A}_t$ via GAE. (3) For $K$ epochs, sample minibatches from the collected data and perform SGD on $L^{\mathrm{CLIP+VF+S}}$. (4) Update $\theta_{\text{old}} \leftarrow \theta$ and repeat.

nodes.name: Clipped objective as lower bound (informal)
nodes.statement: For any $\theta$, $L^{\mathrm{CLIP}}(\theta) \le L^{\mathrm{CPI}}(\theta)$. When $\hat{A}_t > 0$, the objective is $\min(r_t, 1+\epsilon) \hat{A}_t$, preventing overly large increases in probability ratio. When $\hat{A}_t < 0$, the objective is $\max(r_t, 1-\epsilon) \hat{A}_t$, preventing the ratio from decreasing too much. This provides a pessimistic bound analogous to the trust-region constraint.
conclusions: $L^{\mathrm{CLIP}} \le L^{\mathrm{CPI}}$ pointwise, providing a pessimistic lower bound
Gradient of $L^{\mathrm{CLIP}}$ is zero when $r_t$ is clipped, preventing large updates

nodes.name: Atari benchmark results
nodes.statement: PPO with the clipped objective achieves performance competitive with or superior to A2C, ACER, and TRPO across 49 Atari games, while being substantially simpler to implement. PPO-Clip outperforms PPO-Penalty and standard policy gradient methods.

nodes.name: Continuous control (MuJoCo) results
nodes.statement: On continuous control tasks (Hopper, Walker, HalfCheetah, Swimmer, etc.), PPO matches or exceeds TRPO performance while requiring only first-order optimization (no conjugate gradient or Fisher-vector products).
